svg.aria-label: BCBC 2024 Article 9.9.6.5 Direction of Door Swing
svg.title: BCBC 2024 · 9.9.6.5 Direction of Door Swing
svg.text: BCBC 2024 · DIVISION B · PART 9 HOUSING AND SMALL BUILDINGS · SECTION 9.9 MEANS OF EGRESS
Direction of Door Swing

g.text: From a room with an occupant load
over 60: swings on the vertical axis
in the direction of exit travel
Doors dividing a corridor not wholly within
a suite: swing in the direction of exit travel
SENTENCE (4): A PAIR OF DOORS IN A CORRIDOR WITH EXITS IN BOTH DIRECTIONS (PLANS)
(a) Opposite swings: the door on the right-hand side
swings in the direction of exit travel
(b) The doors swing in both directions

svg.text: WHAT THE CODE REQUIRES
Exit doors that are required to swing, swing
in the direction of exit travel
Except doors serving a single dwelling unit or a
house with a secondary suite, including their
common spaces.
Doors that open onto a corridor or other
facility that provides access to exit from a
room or suite with an occupant load of more
than 60 persons swing on the vertical axis in
the direction of exit travel
Doors that divide a corridor that is not
wholly contained within a suite swing in the
direction of exit travel
Where a pair of doors is installed in a
corridor that provides access to exit in both
directions, the doors
(a) swing in opposite directions, with the door
on the right-hand side swinging in the direction
of exit travel, or (b) swing in both directions.
Drawn: a corridor leading to an exit (pink), front wall cut low, doors part open. Green arrows: exit travel.
Source: BCBC 2024, Division B, Article 9.9.6.5. (page 9-50)
